title: Auto-Tune grew out of maths used to hunt for oil underground
body: Engineer Andy Hildebrand spent years in the oil industry interpreting seismic data, using sound waves bounced through rock to map possible oil deposits. He realised the same signal-processing maths, especially a technique called autocorrelation, could track the pitch of a voice in real time. His company Antares released Auto-Tune in 1997 to discreetly fix off-key notes, and Cher’s 1998 hit Believe made its robotic extreme setting famous.
